verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Both clauses are stated, as two declarations rather than one display. Smoothness: `source_smooth` gives ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ of `residualSource`, whose codomain `ComplexVector = Fin 3 → ℂ` is the paper's ℂ³; it is proved on `ActualInitialization.geometry.domain` rather than on a per-label enlarged domain, and it carries two hypotheses on the carrier family (closedness, and positive radius on the domain) which `ActualParticularCycleData.native_source_smooth` (line 140) discharges with `ActualCoreSupport.refinedCarrier`, giving smoothness on the native chart domain. Support: the Lean clause is the germ statement `source_zero_germ`, that the coefficient vanishes on a whole neighbourhood of every domain point outside `labelCarrier l n` (ActualInitialExcluded.lean:730, the label's slow mask and Gaussian source rectangle); that is at least as strong as the inclusion supp ⊆ Ω_γ inside the domain, and it is also what the paper's following sentence about smooth zero extension asks for. `native_source_exterior` is the same vanishing in the native chart, outside the radial window. What I did not do is identify the Lean sets with the paper's: I compared the shape of the two statements, not `geometry.domain` against ℰ_γ⁺ or `labelCarrier l n` against Ω_γ of (6.28).
